Subject: Request: Clarify invoicing flow & VAT split for AWS Marketplace co-sell purchase

Hi Chloe,

We have a multi-entity purchase coming through AWS Marketplace for one of our business units. Procurement needs clarity on two items before we proceed:

1) Invoicing path: will the invoice arrive from AWS (marketplace) directly to CloudCorp, or will Redwood be able to supply a separate invoice that maps charges back to our legal entities? We have a couple of internal procurement rules that require specific vendor invoices.

2) VAT / tax handling: for EU-based subsidiaries we need to confirm whether VAT is charged on the marketplace invoice or whether we should apply reverse charge and self-account — and what evidence Redwood provides (VAT IDs, reverse-charge language) when settlement flows via the marketplace.

Also: do we need W-8/W-9 forms from Redwood if Redwood is listed in the marketplace but AWS is the transacting party? If you can share a short matrix or sample invoice lines it would be helpful.

Can you loop in whoever handles marketplace billing? We have a short timeline (deal committed next week).

Subject: Re: Request: Clarify invoicing flow & VAT split for AWS Marketplace co-sell purchase

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear list. High level answers up front, then a short mapping and attachments: 

TL;DR:
- Default: AWS/GCP/Azure (marketplace) issues the invoice to the customer when the purchase is consumed via the marketplace public listing. Redwood receives settlement from the marketplace and does NOT normally issue a customer-facing invoice in that path.
- Exceptions: If you need an invoice directly from Redwood, we can support that only for private offers / seller-of-record arrangements or when the marketplace flow is configured for seller invoice (varies by cloud). That typically requires a contract amendment and coordination with the marketplace team.
- VAT: For EU customers on marketplace invoices, VAT treatment depends on where the transaction is deemed to occur and the configured seller. If the marketplace is the billing party, the marketplace will usually charge VAT per their rules. If Redwood is the seller of record, we can issue VAT-inclusive invoices or provide reverse-charge wording and compute net amounts when customers qualify.
- W-8 / W-9: If the marketplace is the transacting party (AWS invoicing you), marketplace withholding rules apply and you generally do not need our W-9. If Redwood invoices you directly (seller-of-record/private offer), we will provide the appropriate W-9/W-8 forms on request.

Attached: Marketplace_Invoicing_Mapping.xlsx (quick matrix with AWS/Azure/GCP flows), W9_W8_Checklist.pdf, and a sample AWS marketplace invoice line so you can see the line-level format.

Short mapping (see attachment for full table):
- Public listing (standard marketplace): Marketplace invoices customer; invoice shows product code and gross amount; VAT applied by marketplace. Redwood gets settlement report and pays out via marketplace settlement.
- Private offer / Seller of Record: Redwood invoices customer directly; Redwood is responsible for VAT/tax treatment; will provide VAT number and full invoice lines; customer can receive separate legal invoices per entity if we set up multi-entity invoicing (requires finance integration & PO routing).
- Co-sell (AWS): If AWS co-sell with marketplace lead, often AWS still invoices; some co-sell programs allow seller-provided invoicing if the offer is a private offer with Seller of Record set to Redwood.

Action items I propose:
1) Jordan — confirm whether CloudCorp needs Redwood-native invoices (yes/no) for each legal entity, or if AWS marketplace invoice is acceptable.
2) If Redwood invoices required: CloudCorp to confirm entity mapping and PO routing per attachment.
3) Stephanie / Finance: help confirm whether we can enable per-entity invoice splitting for this account under our current marketplace setup and what lead time is required.

If helpful I can host a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the team through the attachment.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Partnerships Manager, Marketplace
Redwood Inference

Jordan / J — looping in Stephanie (Marketplace Partnerships lead) and Dev (Finance integrations) to confirm the minimal path and timelines. Quick answers + proposed next steps below.

Short answers:
- Per-entity invoice split from the marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure) is not reliably supported for public listings — marketplaces tend to issue a single invoice per customer account. Splitting by legal entity on a single marketplace invoice is uncommon unless the buyer creates separate marketplace accounts per entity.
- To get Redwood-native, per-entity invoices you will need a private offer (Seller of Record or Seller-Invoicing enabled). That requires: 
  * Marketplace private-offer configuration (takes ~2-4 weeks to coordinate in our experience)
  * Contract amendment to set Redwood as seller-of-record / invoicing party or a channel reseller setup
  * Finance integration for multi-entity PO routing (Dev will scope)
- If your accounting team will accept AWS marketplace invoice + settlement reports, you can avoid the conversion. In that case we can provide:
  * Detailed settlement reports mapping usage to our internal product codes (attachment),
  * VAT evidence (our VAT ID and language templates) that you can attach for reverse-charge positions,
  * W-9: Not provided for marketplace-transacted invoices (AWS is transacting party). If you require Redwood W-9 regardless, we can provide it, but note it does not change the tax withholding that AWS applies.

Proposed next steps (pick A or B):
A) Fast path (if marketplace invoice acceptable):
  - We send a sample AWS marketplace invoice and settlement mapping (attached).
  - CloudCorp confirms acceptance and AP routing rule updates.
  - Timeline: same week.

B) Redwood invoice per entity (private offer path):
  - CloudCorp confirms entity mapping + PO numbers per-entity (use column B in attached XLSX).
  - Redwood legal drafts addendum and we initiate private offer with AWS; Finance will confirm lead times.
  - Estimated lead time: 2-4 weeks + contract signatures.

Dev: can you confirm the systems work needed (ERP PO routing + OASIS/NetSuite mapping) and an estimated work effort? Stephanie: any red flags on contract side if customer requests seller-of-record for this deal?

Thanks — happy to take a call.

Best,
Chloe
